title: Strong converse for the quantum capacity of the pure-loss bosonic channel
abstract: This paper reports the proof of a strong converse for the unconstrained quantum capacity of the pure-loss bosonic channel. At every fixed rate above capacity, the entanglement-generation fidelity of every code is bounded by a constant times the reciprocal of the number of channel uses. The bound holds without an energy constraint and for arbitrary encoded states, including states correlated across all input modes, and arbitrary joint decoders. The proof combines quantum Chebyshev and hockey-stick testing inequalities with a uniform relative-entropy-variance bound for the balanced pure-loss channel, corresponding to transmissivity $η=1/2$. The variance bound follows by expressing the balanced beam splitter in bright and dark modes: the dark modes are exactly in vacuum, and any state orthogonal to that vacuum contains at least one dark photon. For general transmissivity, dilating the degrading attenuator reduces the problem to this balanced-channel setting and bounds the decoder test by precisely the factor that produces the known quantum-capacity threshold. The resulting argument establishes the strong converse at the unconstrained quantum capacity for every pure-loss bosonic channel.
summary: This paper rigorously proves a strong converse for the quantum capacity of the pure-loss bosonic channel. It shows that if the transmission rate exceeds the channel capacity, the achievable fidelity of any quantum code decays polynomially with the block length. The work employs advanced techniques from quantum information theory, linking channel loss to fundamental bounds on quantum state estimation.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a strong converse for the unconstrained quantum capacity of the pure-loss bosonic channel.
main_result: It proves that for any rate above capacity, the entanglement-generation fidelity of any code decays polynomially ($O(1/n)$) with the number of channel uses $n$.
method: The proof combines quantum Chebyshev and hockey-stick testing inequalities with a uniform relative-entropy-variance bound, reducing the general case to the balanced-channel setting.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the pure-loss bosonic channel, which describes optical attenuation via a beam-splitter mixing an input mode with a vacuum mode.
key_observables: Entanglement-generation fidelity of codes, the rate gap ($\delta_n$), and the quantum capacity ($q_\eta$).
important_parameters: Transmissivity ($\eta$), the number of channel uses ($n$), and the rate ($\log_2 M$).
main_assumptions: The proof is for the *unconstrained* quantum capacity and establishes a polynomial decay rate, not an exponential one.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates two equivalent vacuum-fed beam-splitter dilations for $1/2 < \eta < 1$, relating the pure-loss model to a balanced beam splitter.
paper_structure: The argument develops by first establishing tools like the logarithmic trace inequality, then analyzing the balanced-channel state, and finally extending the bound to general transmissivities and arbitrary input states.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous, quantitative bounds on the fundamental limits of quantum communication through lossy optical channels, which is crucial for quantum networking and quantum optics.
